titulo_en: Exact and heuristic methods for solving the family traveling salesman problem
resumo_en: In the field of Operations Research, one trend is the development of hybrid exact and heuristic methods to obtain good-quality results for combinatorial optimization problems. There are several ways to hybridize. One way to hybridize exact methods is to integrate an exact method with local search heuristics. A hybrid version of metaheuristics can be obtained by integrating Machine Learning techniques. One of the most classic combinatorial optimization problems is the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP). In this problem, only the operational costs involved in the salesman's route are minimized. However, the TSP can be adapted to different problems faced by logistics companies, such as different product categories, delivery priorities, and product locations in warehouses. This work addresses the Family Traveling Salesman Problem (FTSP), in which customers are grouped into families that correspond to products of the same similarity and with a predefined number of required visits. The goal of the FTSP is to determine the minimum-cost route visiting only a subset of customers from each family. Like the TSP, it is a combinatorial optimization problem belonging to the NP-hard class. To solve the proposed problem, two methods were developed: (i) a parallel branch-and-cut with an efficient local search procedure to obtain the optimal solution, and (ii) an adaptive metaheuristic that combines the Biased Random-Key Genetic Algorithm (BRKGA) with a reinforcement learning algorithm, Q-Learning (QL). In this case, the Q-Learning algorithm is used to control the BRKGA parameters during the evolutionary process. Computational experiments were carried out on a well-known benchmark dataset with 185 instances. The P-B&C algorithm developed for the FTSP proves the optimal value for 179 instances, and BRKGA-QL found the best upper bounds for the other four instances. The results were compared with the best results in the literature, and both methods show robustness and efficiency in solving the FTSP.

titulo_en: Parametric model for preliminary cost estimation in the product development process
resumo_en: The high level of competitiveness that characterizes the aeronautical industry, combined with the manufacturing complexity inherent to products in this sector, makes it relevant to study methods and techniques capable of producing information with the highest possible degree of accuracy throughout a product's development cycle. The most significant design and configuration decisions for a new product are made in the early phases of the development cycle, where the level of detail is inherently low. However, these decisions commit around 80% of the product's costs, which makes them critical. In this context, promoting the use of an efficient preliminary cost estimation method that supports the critical decisions made at the start of a product's development is consistent with companies' need to become more competitive. This work proposes using the parametric method of multiple regression analysis, based on a historical dataset of aircraft from the Brazilian company Embraer, to estimate the costs of a specific structural component (the wing box), in order to validate the use of this estimation model in the early phases of an aeronautical product's development. The results indicate that the proposed method is satisfactory, meeting qualitative and quantitative evaluation criteria related to, for example, ease of application and interpretation, use of input data available in the early development phases, and accuracy of the resulting estimates. As a follow-up to this work, we suggest integrating the resulting cost estimation model with stochastic optimization and multidisciplinary design optimization (MDO) processes, to be carried out during the sizing of a new aircraft in its early development phases.

titulo_en: Optimized selection of unstable links in ATN/IPS aeronautical communication networks
resumo_en: Aeronautical communications under the new ATN-Br (Aeronautical Telecommunication Network - Brazil) concept introduce a new, exclusively digital communication model. As a result, network management becomes essential to ensure the continuity of communications. In this context, the heterogeneous network selection techniques found in the literature are a way to perform link selection based on criteria that meet the requirements of the communication services and of the users of this aeronautical network. The objective of this work is to present an integrated optimization model to select the links of the aeronautical network, maximizing network usage and minimizing the difference in capacity usage between links (load balancing). To achieve this, multicriteria evaluation techniques are combined with a multiobjective optimization method. The AHP (Analytic Hierarchy Process) method is used to analyze subjective criteria, and utility functions are used for objective criteria. The criteria are combined using the compensatory multicriteria method SAW (Simple Additive Weighting) to evaluate the possible combinations of links and packets. The epsilon-constraint multiobjective optimization provides Pareto-optimal frontier values as balancing levels (difference between link occupancy rates) are defined for the network. The link selection problem is addressed through a case study, with data generated from real ATN-Br data. The results of this case study indicate that there is an operating point (trade-off) that maximizes network usage (profit) and minimizes the difference in link usage (difference between the occupancy rates of the available bands), without increasing packet loss. Thus, the proposed solution offers network managers a reference for the optimized operation of the ATN-Br, ensuring the continuity of the most critical (priority) communications, including in scenarios of link instability.

titulo_en: A participatory process to make Brazilian Air Force mission models and simulations faithful to its demands
resumo_en: The Brazilian Air Force (FAB) has been increasingly adopting simulators to support decision-making at the strategic and operational levels. These tools allow the evaluation of new systems, improvements, and changes to the Force's doctrines, tactics, and techniques. To define how simulations will be conducted, it is necessary to capture from stakeholders what their needs are and how their fulfillment should be measured. This work presents a process to improve fidelity, through facilitation and increased participation, so that stakeholders can indicate to modelers and system architects the context of the problem situation and the problems themselves, whose solutions should become desirable emergent properties, and validate each step of the process, with the final goal of developing a simulation engine that meets the expectations of the parties involved. The process was developed with a multimethodology that combines different paradigms: i) Conceptual Modeling in Discrete-Event Simulation and Soft Operational Research; and ii) Executable Architectures and Model-Based Systems Engineering. On this basis, a Participatory Conceptual Modeling process to make FAB Mission Simulations faithful to its demands (MPSM) was structured, capable of: i) involving stakeholders throughout the entire simulation life cycle, addressing their objectives and needs; ii) maintaining the traceability and validity of the model elements; iii) enabling future semi-automation of simulations; iv) developing an executable architecture from the modeling, using a Model-Based Systems Engineering tool. The MPSM was built in successive parts and verified by applying its parts during 2021 and 2022 in space, cyber, and drone operation projects. These applications show the relationships between the tools and methods of Critical Systems Heuristics (CSH), Soft Systems Methodology (SSM), Participative Simulation (PartSim), Hierarchical Control Conceptual Modeling (HCCM), and Arcadia, which were used to structure the MPSM. They thus show that, together, they form "a whole greater than the sum of its parts".

titulo_en: Comparison of different time series forecasting approaches: a study of production consumption in the Brazilian aeronautical sector
resumo_en: The aeronautical sector is an essential part of the Brazilian industrial landscape, playing a crucial role in the development of new technologies and production practices that apply to many industries. In this context, studying and implementing improvements to existing systems is highly valuable. One area with great potential for improvement is production planning, especially where forecasting techniques are applied within the supply chain. The main objective of this study is to compare several time series forecasting approaches, covering classical statistical methods, neural networks, and a hybrid approach. To evaluate the effectiveness of these models, different evaluation metrics are applied, including sMAPE, Theil's Inequality Coefficient, RMSE, and the Dowdall Rule. The application scenario consists of real time series representing the consumption of electrical hardware materials used on the production line of a Brazilian aircraft manufacturer. This study aims to contribute to improving the application of time series forecasting methods in a real-world context.

titulo_en: Fatigue life prediction of joints for aeronautical applications based on the stress severity factor
resumo_en: The objective of this work is to investigate the validity limits and the degree of conservatism in predicting the fatigue life of aeronautical fuselage joints, using the stress severity factor as the method for obtaining the Kt to be applied to the S-N curve of the plate material. To this end, results from fatigue tests were compared with those obtained using the investigated method. Finite element models were built to obtain the load distribution in the fasteners and to measure the stress due to secondary bending. The method proved conservative for about 74% of the joints analyzed, showing robustness in predicting the fatigue life of lap joints. Only two of six asymmetric butt joint configurations were covered by the method, highlighting the need to include the effect of secondary bending when the eccentricity between the joint's neutral line and the load application line increases.

titulo_en: Interpretable generative model for estimating latent variables for response assessment
resumo_en: In recent years, a growing trend in machine learning has been the development of more interpretable models capable of explaining their predictions. This emerging field of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) has focused mainly on explaining supervised models, which is a paradox, since unsupervised models are precisely the ones that most require interpretability so that their results can be effectively understood and validated. In this context, this thesis proposes an interpretable unsupervised generative model for estimating latent variables, which are information not directly observable in the data but inferred from underlying patterns. However, unlike typical unsupervised learning approaches such as clustering algorithms, the proposal does not aim to segment instances and interpret them, but rather to reveal latent dimensions that can be extracted from the data with a measurable meaning. This proposal generalizes Item Response Theory (IRT) models, overcoming their structural limitations and lack of flexibility, while incorporating transparency and interpretability mechanisms into the process. Different applications were explored to validate the proposal. The first was in the domain of personalized education, demonstrating its performance through a practical example based on the Brazilian National High School Exam (ENEM). Overall, the proposal achieved good results, producing a better determination of the probability of answering an item correctly compared with simply using probabilities of a correct answer conditioned on the respondent's abilities. The second application addressed the assessment of the difficulty level of observations in datasets for classification problems. Simulated scenarios, traditional machine learning datasets, and specific healthcare problems were considered, notably datasets related to COVID-19 and Dengue lethality. In all these situations, the results showed that the proposed approach makes it possible to quantify instance difficulty, contributing to a deeper understanding of the data structure and of the performance of predictive models. The experiments confirm the effectiveness of the proposed interpretable generative model in extracting and interpreting latent variables in an unsupervised manner.

titulo_en: Multimethodological approach to landslide prevention in a city in the interior of the State of São Paulo
resumo_en: Due to its tropical climate, high summer rainfall, and mountainous areas, Brazil faces significant challenges related to landslides. This problem is characterized by its complexity, owing to the interactions among various elements, uncertainties, the diversity of actors and perspectives, and the unpredictable impacts that affect the system as a whole. In this context, the objective of this work was to develop a methodological framework to establish strategic actions that contribute to landslide prevention. A case study was carried out in the city of Campos do Jordão, focusing on the Britador neighborhood, chosen for its proximity to where the researcher lives and because it is prone to landslides due to its mountainous topography and the region's climatic characteristics. The research adopted a qualitative approach, using Problem Structuring Methods derived from Soft Operational Research, through a multimethodological approach applying Soft Systems Methodology together with Value-Focused Thinking. Data were obtained from a variety of sources, including news, reports, social media, a literature review, and semi-structured interviews with open questions. Interviews were conducted with a representative of the Civil Defense, a representative of the Department of the Environment, a representative of the Department of Urban Services, a representative of the Department of Social Assistance, two representatives of residents/merchants of the Britador neighborhood in Campos do Jordão, and a representative of tourists. The intended result was a detailed description of the actions that would improve the landslide prevention process in Campos do Jordão. This included proposing the construction of new housing to replace homes located in landslide-prone areas, regularizing housing in low-risk areas, improving the drainage system, among other measures aimed at benefiting the population and, above all, saving lives.

titulo_en: Modeling and solving the robust unequal-area facility layout problem with input and output locations
resumo_en: One of the strategies used to optimize production processes is defining the best physical arrangement. Many companies therefore study the relative positioning of their equipment, areas, or functional activities. An appropriate arrangement of facilities can result in shorter process times and higher productivity of the production factors. In general, the objective of the facility layout problem is to reduce material handling cost, which can be represented by a function relating material flows to the distances between facilities. The dynamic facility layout problem considers a multi-period planning horizon in which material flows between pairs of facilities may change over time, and it can be solved with a flexible or a robust approach. A flexible plant can accept changes in facility positions over time to follow demand changes, as long as this offsets the relocation costs, whereas a robust plant is a single layout solution that may not be excellent for any individual scenario but seeks to be the best when the scenarios are evaluated together. Considering a dynamic demand environment, this work carried out a robust rather than flexible analysis, since rearrangement and production interruption costs are high and an adaptive approach can be too inconvenient in an industry's routine. Within the layout problem there are little-explored aspects that were addressed in this research, namely unequal-area blocks, input and output locations in the blocks, fixed facilities or occupied spaces, and clearance distances around facilities. In this context, new mixed-integer programming mathematical models for the facility layout problem were developed and validated, based on an analysis of models proposed in the literature. As an alternative for implementation in modeling programs and mathematical software, these models were also linearized. To provide solutions to the modeled problems, several solution methods involving mathematical programming and heuristics were developed and applied, achieving good results on different instances from the literature.

titulo_en: Application of an agent-based model to simulate the radio frequency auction process in Brazil
resumo_en: This dissertation addresses the notable gap in applying Agent-Based Models (ABM) to the study of spectrum auctions in Brazil, focusing specifically on the 5G Auction. The main purpose of the study is to analyze the influence of the number of participating companies and their degree of aggressiveness on the individual results of each lot and on the overall auction result, by creating a simulator that reproduces the rules of the latest spectrum auction held in Brazil, the 5G Auction. As the results indicate, both the number of participating companies and the aggressiveness of the bids significantly affect the auction outcomes. The study emphasizes the importance of considering both factors when planning auctions and developing bidding strategies. However, it must be recognized that, although powerful, Agent-Based Modeling is highly dependent on the assumptions and rules established in the model, which limits the generalization of the results to other contexts or countries. This research extends the academic literature in telecommunications and behavioral economics, offering an analysis of the strategies and behaviors of auction participants. Furthermore, the study can help telecommunications policymakers and regulators design more efficient and fair spectrum auctions.

titulo_en: Comparison of prognostic methods for the crew oxygen system of a commercial aircraft
resumo_en: This work presents a comparative study of prognostic fusion methodologies aimed at improving the prediction of a system's state, thereby supporting decision-making for critical equipment. First, a brief introduction to the main prognostic tools is given, along with recommendations on which to use in each situation. Then a case study of the crew oxygen system is carried out, comparing four different techniques for fusing the estimates of several tools used individually: mean, median, neural networks, and weighted mean. It is concluded that there is no single "best" approach, since this varies from case to case. Factors that can influence the final result are computational capacity, prediction quality, and the confidence interval of the predictions.

titulo_en: An interactive and flexible TRADEOFF aggregation method for group decision-making
resumo_en: This work stems from the need to develop a flexible and interactive method for group decision-making that considers the strength of preference of each decision-maker during the elicitation of scaling constants, within a multicriteria decision context, without necessarily weighting each decision-maker during the process. To achieve these goals, the concept of flexible and interactive Tradeoff was used, which is grounded in Multi-Attribute Value Theory and helps individuals assign values to scaling constants in a multicriteria model with reduced cognitive effort. To support this process with multiple decision-makers, a hybrid method combining FITradeoff with the construction of second-order preference functions was applied. This method allows decision-makers to interact continuously with the flexible Tradeoff procedure, while in each choice cycle the heuristic is adjusted based on each decision-maker's strength of preference. This hybrid method allows the decision-makers' judgments to be aggregated while they make their individual choices, rather than only aggregating the final preferences and their individual weight vectors or spaces. Besides structuring the scaling constant elicitation model, the hybrid method allows investigating the construction of second-order preference functions in an additive aggregation model within the multicriteria decision context. As a final contribution, a structured method with an execution algorithm is provided, combining these features. An example is implemented in which four decision-makers took part in the process, interacting with the previously structured model and converging to a choice among four alternatives with respect to four criteria, with a single solution at the end.

titulo_en: NSGA-II for the efficient solution of multiobjective routing problems in wireless sensor networks
resumo_en: In recent years, there has been an increase in the use of applications and new technologies of wireless sensor networks (WSNs), which perform event monitoring tasks in different environments. WSNs thus allow information from the physical environment to be connected to the Internet, making them an essential part of the Internet of Things (IoT) concept. A WSN consists basically of low-cost microdevices with limited energy reserves (called sensors), capable of collecting, transmitting, and receiving data. It is fundamentally important to find ways and solutions that meet the intrinsic needs related to the technological limitations of the network components, such as maximizing the network's energy efficiency, minimizing the percentage of information loss, maximizing network coverage, among other characteristics called quality metrics. This Master's dissertation addresses a bi-objective routing problem in WSNs recently proposed in the literature, whose optimization criteria are two conflicting quality metrics among the most emphasized in the literature: residual energy efficiency and data delivery reliability. The heuristic approach used in the literature was unable to obtain results for large-scale environments. Moreover, for both small- and large-scale environments, the literature heuristic produced sparse Pareto curves, making it difficult to evaluate the results. To solve the problem, this dissertation adapted the multiobjective evolutionary algorithm Elitist Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm (NSGA-II). Simulation results show that solving the problem with NSGA-II is more effective in terms of solution quality and computational time than the exact and heuristic approaches from the literature. In addition, given the good performance obtained in small-scale environments with the evolutionary approach, it was possible to solve the bi-objective problem in large-scale environments with solutions in feasible computational time.

titulo_en: Value-focused objectives in defining soft systems methodology actions: a case study on the inclusion of students with specific educational needs
resumo_en: Real-world problems are complex; this complexity translates into a lack of elements that would allow defining objectives, constraints, and resources, as well as what the actual problem to be considered is. Moreover, such problems may require broad changes in policies, assumptions, and underlying objectives, which makes it necessary to define not only the problems to be addressed but also the objectives they affect. Educational support for students with specific educational needs is a complex problem with context-dependent dynamics that is difficult to address. The purpose of this study is to develop an approach that makes it possible to identify and define undesired states in a given problem situation and to plan models that lead to a more desirable state in accordance with the objectives of those involved. To achieve this, an approach based on problem structuring methods was built that allows: abstracting the context of the problem situation under consideration; defining objectives based on the values of those involved; and steering the situation toward changes aligned with the defined objectives. The approach was applied in an educational unit to address educational support for students with specific educational needs. Applying the approach brought benefits such as a clear definition of how education for these students is understood in the institution: special attention to the target population regardless of a clinical report. It also made it possible to identify the real problems and objectives, deconstructing established concepts. This study contributes to the Operations Research literature by guiding systemic planning through objectives based on the values of those involved. This contribution makes it possible to set boundaries, guide, and prioritize the planning of necessary changes. As a social contribution, the study provides a structured means of identifying the practices needed for the effective inclusion of students with specific educational needs.

titulo_en: Optimization under uncertainty: a new computational method, a new robustness measure, and applications
resumo_en: The currently most popular approach to help decision-makers handle uncertainty in linear and integer optimization problems has the drawback of requiring an uncertainty control parameter that is not always trivial to choose. This work presents three advances in this area: 1) development of an approach to solve optimization problems under uncertainty, applying the developed method to an Industry 4.0 linear optimization problem (bandwidth packing) and comparing it with an approach from the literature; 2) modeling and solving a nonlinear 2D target localization problem under uncertainty using distance geometry, comparing it with an approach from the literature; and 3) creating a feasibility-based quality measure and validating it on a classic linear optimization problem from the literature. The method for solving optimization problems under uncertainty proposed in this thesis, called SIROM (Sampling-based multi-objective Iterative Robust Optimization Method), was designed to automatically find solutions to optimization problems under uncertainty using the information obtained during a simulation process and the clustering of solutions by similarity. Its application to the bandwidth problem obtained results better than or equal to those of the literature method for the same problem in 92.53% of the instances. The modeling of the 2D target localization problem considered a different definition of the type of uncertainty used in the classic literature model, and its solution found a lower localization error in 59.3% of the cases, as well as a shorter execution time. In addition, a new robustness measure called Hardness was created, which considers the feasibility of a solution for any realization of the uncertain parameters and, by accounting for the difference in robustness between solutions, proved clearer than the quality measures in the literature.

titulo_en: New flow formulations for combinatorial optimization problems
resumo_en: This work addresses the Tool Switching Minimization Problem (ToSP) and the Multiproduct Traveling Salesman Problem with Priorities. The ToSP consists of determining a job sequence such that the number of tool switches between jobs is as small as possible. Each job requires a distinct set of tools, and each of these sets is assumed to contain no more tools than the machine can hold. The Multiproduct Traveling Salesman Problem with Priorities consists of determining a goods delivery route that considers both the customer and the seller at the same time, that is, minimizing the seller's total costs and maximizing customer preferences. The objective of this study is to model these problems based on multicommodity flow. Mathematical optimization models were proposed and some theoretical results were developed. For the ToSP, the best proposed model was compared with existing models in the literature, showing better performance in the number of instances solved to optimality, in the linear relaxation value, and in execution time. It was shown that the linear relaxation value of the proposed models corresponds to the difference between the number of tools and the machine capacity. Some matheuristics based on proximity search and an exact enumerative method with symmetry elimination were proposed and compared with results from the literature. For the Multiproduct Traveling Salesman Problem with Priorities, the proposed model proved efficient in solving small and medium-sized instances. Two metaheuristics, BRKGA and adaptive BRKGA, both with local search, were also proposed for this problem, showing good results.
